findings.F1: The rebound after a 24-hour drop is a high-volatility effect. On the 48-hour non-overlapping grid, drops of at least 2 multiples of the 30-day average absolute daily return gave +3.24 % unusual move in the coin's own top volatility tercile (t 4.49, 239 cases, strength 0.45). The middle tercile gave +0.19 % (t 0.44, 361 cases) and the bottom tercile −0.23 % (t −0.79, 414 cases).
findings.F2: The same split holds when volatility is measured against the coin's own past, using its 30-day average absolute daily return over its 180-day mean. Drops of at least 2 multiples gave +2.26 % over 48 hours in the top tercile (t 4.76, 233 cases), +0.02 % in the middle (t 0.03) and −0.32 % in the bottom (t −0.68). Over 96 hours the top tercile gave +4.21 % (t 3.28, 114 cases).
findings.F3: Inside high volatility the rebound is graded. The slope of 48-hour strength on the size of the drop is 0.32 (t 3.59) in the top volatility tercile, 0.19 (t 3.30) in the middle and 0.05 (t 1.58) in the bottom.
findings.F4: The high-volatility rebound is broad but not steady.
findings.F5: The rebound is far larger than the cost of a trade. In the top volatility tercile the total 48-hour move per case is +2.6 % to +3.2 % against a 0.22 % round trip, 12 to 15 times the cost. Over all drops of at least 2 multiples the unusual move is +0.56 %, 2.5 times the cost.
findings.F6: Unconditional drops are not graded. Across all volatility levels, drops of 2 to 3 multiples gave −0.10 % over 48 hours (t −0.35, 669 cases), while drops beyond 3 multiples gave +2.3 % to +2.4 % (t 3.3 to 3.6, 345 cases). Most of the tested idea's edge therefore sits in a few large, high-volatility drops.
findings.F7: The book earned 0.04 % a day against 0.15 % for holding (daily sd 1.6 % vs 5.7 %). Its trades held up to 2 days averaged +2.9 % net (6,753 trades). Trades held 3 to 5 days averaged −3.8 % (1,913) and 5 to 10 days −3.3 % (1,649). Holding past the 2-day horizon when the forecast stays on cost the book.
findings.F8: Large 24-hour rises in the coin's low-volatility tercile gave +1.07 % over 48 hours (t 3.63, 530 cases, 15 of 19 coins). The result is not robust:
findings.F9: Large 24-hour rises when the 30-day return is negative gave −0.89 % over 48 hours (t −2.37, 319 cases). Hour of day (block 04–08 UTC: +2.7 %, t 2.47, 110 cases) and past 7-day return quintiles showed nothing graded. Given the number of angles looked at, none of these stands out from chance.

ideas.idea: When a coin's average absolute daily return over the last 30 days is high relative to its own level over the past 6 months, a 24-hour drop measured in multiples of that average is followed by a rise over the next 2 days above the coin's usual 2-day drift. The larger the drop in multiples and the higher the coin's recent volatility relative to its past, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A sharp 24-hour plunge is a reason to buy for two days when the coin is already in an unusually volatile stretch, and a reason to stand aside when it comes in a calm one.
ideas.name: high-volatility plunge two-day rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin's average absolute daily return over the last 30 days is high relative to its own level over the past 6 months, a 24-hour drop measured in multiples of that average is followed by a rise over the next 4 days above the coin's usual 4-day drift. The larger the drop and the higher the relative volatility, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: In a volatile stretch, a plunge bought and held for four days captures a move many times the cost of a round trip.
ideas.name: high-volatility plunge four-day rebound
